categories_checked.note: Lånekassen: EEA/EFTA citizen rules, foreign-national rules, university support page, 2026-2027 rates news item.
Husbanken bostøtte (housing allowance) student rules: students with a right to Lånekassen support are excluded. No municipal student rent subsidy found in Oslo.
SiO Health refund of GP user fees above NOK 490/year for SiO students with a SiO GP.
Ruter 40% student discount on the 30-day ticket (Oslo/Akershus).
Skatteetaten exemption card (frikort): income up to NOK 100,000/year tax free, only for persons staying in Norway a full year.
Searched UiO part-time work page, Skatteetaten study page and Arbeidstilsynet: no subsidy specific to working students found (only rules, see bureaucracy.json).

UiO: incoming Erasmus, Nordplus/Nordlys and most bilateral exchange students are exempt from the semester fee. No host-country Erasmus top-up found; incoming Erasmus grants are paid by the home country.
No Oslo municipality or county grant for students found on the pages checked (SiO, UiO, Husbanken). Search budget ran out before a dedicated search of oslo.kommune.no.
UiO: tuition fee exemptions (residence/ties-based); UiO states it has no scholarships covering tuition. SiO welfare services funded by the semester fee.

items.name_it: Sostegno Lånekassen per cittadini UE/SEE con status di lavoratore
items.description: EEA/EFTA citizens can get Norwegian student finance as workers: either by keeping a job of at least 10 hours/week while studying, or by leaving a job in Norway to study a programme professionally linked to that job (link waived after 6 months of involuntary unemployment registered with Nav). Eligibility ends when you lose worker status.

eligibility.min_work_hours: at least 10 hours/week of employment in Norway while studying, or employment ended to study with a professional link to the programme
eligibility.income_test: Grant conversion only if income below NOK 234,821 (2026) and assets below the limit
eligibility.residence_requirement: None stated for this route; family members of the worker have their own routes
other: Swiss citizens: the Lånekassen page covers EEA/EFTA citizens; EFTA includes Switzerland - confirm with Lånekassen

items.amount: Basic support NOK 15,488/month for full-time students (2026-2027), as a loan; up to 40% can be converted to a grant if you live away from your parents, pass your studies and stay under the income/asset limits
items.how_to_apply: Online application to Lånekassen after admission (from mid-May), with an employer confirmation on letterhead
items.deadline: 15 November (whole year or autumn only); 15 March (spring)
items.notes: The page does not state a minimum duration of prior employment. The 15 Nov / 15 Mar deadlines are on the university support page without a year.

items.name_it: Sostegno Lånekassen per cittadini UE/SEE con diritto di soggiorno permanente
items.description: EEA citizens with a permanent right of residence in Norway (normally after at least 5 years of continuous residence as worker, self-employed, student or with sufficient means) are eligible for Lånekassen support like Norwegian students.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Permanent right of residence in Norway (at least 5 years of continuous residence)
eligibility.income_test: Grant conversion only if income below NOK 234,821 (2026)

items.amount: Basic support NOK 15,488/month for full-time students (2026-2027); up to 40% convertible to a grant
items.how_to_apply: Online application to Lånekassen with proof of permanent residence (residence card or documentation of 5 years' residence)
items.deadline: 15 November (whole year or autumn only); 15 March (spring)

items.name_local: Støtte fra Lånekassen for utenlandske statsborgere
items.description: Non-EU/EEA citizens are generally not eligible on a study permit. Routes exist for permanent residence permit holders, refugees, family immigrants (not joining a student), family of EEA citizens, people with 24 months of continuous full-time work in Norway, or 3 years (180 credits) of completed full-time study in Norway.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Permanent residence permit, protection, family immigration, or 24 months full-time work / 180 credits of prior study in Norway
other: A study permit alone does not appear among the eligible bases

items.amount: Same rates as other students when eligible (NOK 15,488/month basic support, 2026-2027)
items.deadline: 15 November (whole year or autumn only); 15 March (spring)

items.authority: Husbanken (Norwegian State Housing Bank) and municipalities
items.description: Means-tested housing allowance for people with low income and high housing costs. As a rule, students with a right to a loan or grant from Lånekassen (or living with such a student) cannot get it, except e.g. households with children under 18.

eligibility.income_test: Low income relative to housing costs (calculated by Husbanken)
other: Excluded if you have a right to Lånekassen support, unless an exception applies (child under 18 in the household, certain Nav benefits)

items.how_to_apply: Online application to Husbanken / via the municipality

interpretations.hypothesis: Husbanken defines a 'student' as someone in approved education with a right to Lånekassen support and says students denied Lånekassen support can apply; a foreign student without Lånekassen rights could therefore in principle apply.
In practice a foreign student is unlikely to qualify: failing to report a move to the National Registry is a common reason for refusal, and short-stay students are usually not registered as resident.

items.notes: Whether a foreign student on a study permit qualifies was not confirmed; a human should check with Husbanken or the municipality.

items.name_it: SiO Helse - rimborso dei ticket sanitari
items.description: Students who have paid the semester fee and have a SiO GP can claim a refund of GP user fees above NOK 490 per year. Registering with a SiO GP requires a Norwegian national ID number; without one you can still book SiO health appointments by phone.

other: SiO GP (requires a Norwegian national ID number)

items.amount: You pay at most NOK 490/year in GP user fees; SiO covers the rest (year not stated)
items.how_to_apply: Apply to SiO for a refund of healthcare expenses

items.description: 40% discount on the 30-day ticket for full-time students under 30 (only the 30-day ticket).

eligibility.stay_duration: Course of at least 3 months and at least 30 credits per term
other: Full-time student at an institution qualifying for Lånekassen support
Valid student ID for the current term

items.amount: NOK 393 per 30 days in zone 1 (price list from 1 August 2026) instead of NOK 655 adult
items.how_to_apply: Buy in the Ruter app: Period ticket > 30-day ticket > student

interpretations.hypothesis: 'Norwegian student' means enrolled full-time at a Norwegian institution, so foreign degree and full-time exchange students qualify.
The price list footnote ('qualifying for support from Lånekassen') could be read as requiring personal Lånekassen eligibility.

items.notes: Vy (28 Oct 2026) reports the student 30-day ticket became NOK 100 cheaper from 1 Nov 2026 (adult zone 1: NOK 495); the new student price was not found on a Ruter page.

items.description: Income up to NOK 100,000 in a year is tax free with an exemption card, issued automatically and electronically to people over 13. It can only be used by persons who stay in Norway for a full year; above the limit you need a tax deduction card or you are taxed at 50%.

eligibility.stay_duration: Staying in Norway for a full (calendar) year
other: Needs a Norwegian ID number and a job

items.amount: Tax-free income up to NOK 100,000 per year (year not stated on the page; UiO also cites NOK 100,000 per calendar year)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic; view or split it between employers with a Norwegian electronic ID

interpretations.hypothesis: Exchange students staying one semester do not qualify (the card is only for people staying the full year).
UiO states without that caveat that students can earn up to NOK 100,000 tax free in a calendar year.

items.name_local: Fritak fra semesteravgift for innreisende utvekslingsstudenter
items.name_it: Esenzione dalla quota semestrale per studenti Erasmus in entrata (UiO)
items.description: Incoming Erasmus, Nordplus/Nordlys and most bilateral exchange students at UiO do not pay the semester fee (NOK 690 SiO + NOK 220 Kopinor + optional NOK 60 SAIH) and are registered with an exemption automatically; they can still use many SiO welfare offers. No extra host-country Erasmus grant was found.

other: Incoming via Erasmus+, Nordplus/Nordlys or most bilateral agreements

items.amount: Exemption from the semester fee (NOK 970 incl. optional SAIH NOK 60)
items.stackable: Combinable with the Erasmus+ grant paid by the home institution
items.notes: Note: SiO housing requires having paid the semester fee to SiO through your institution; how this applies to fee-exempt exchange students is handled by UiO's housing priority scheme (not checked).

items.description: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss students can be exempted from UiO tuition fees on grounds of residence or ties to Norway (permanent residence, protection, family of an EEA citizen or of a Norwegian, 24 months full-time work, 36 months/180 credits of prior study). UiO says it has no scholarships that cover tuition fees.

eligibility.residence_requirement: One of the listed residence/ties grounds; grounds cannot be combined

items.amount: Full exemption from tuition (UiO master's fees 2026/2027: NOK 136,000-295,000/year)
items.how_to_apply: After accepting the offer, use the online form sent with the invoice and upload documentation
items.deadline: Conditions must be documented by 8 August (autumn) or 10 January (spring) for conditional exemptions

items.name_it: Servizi di welfare SiO (finanziati dalla quota semestrale)
items.description: Paying the semester fee gives access to SiO's welfare services: student housing (students up to 34 at SiO-affiliated institutions), GP, psychologists and counselling at fixed rates or free, and other services. International students can use counselling, psychologists, GPs and dentists at fixed rates or free of charge.

other: Semester fee paid to SiO via the institution (UiO: NOK 690 of the semester fee)

items.amount: SiO share of UiO semester fee: NOK 690 per semester (year not stated)
items.how_to_apply: Pay the semester fee through Studentweb; apply for housing at sio.no (apply early; prioritised by application date)
items.deadline: SiO housing: 1 June for 1 August move-in, 1 November for 2 January move-in (SiO page is not fully consistent; check with SiO)
items.notes: SiO rent levels are not shown in the static pages read today.
